title: Synchronization playbook for ship window and cutoff guardrails (API/Console/Runtime)
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Create a cross-functional playbook that defines the ship window, scope-lock rules, cut criteria, and release notes coordination for the unified release covering Redwood API, Console, and Runtime. The playbook must make explicit the gating criteria for API surface freezes, Console UI/UX toggles, Runtime kernel and quantization changes, and the operational rollout/rollback thresholds that trigger fallbacks. The goal is a predictable, auditable release process that minimizes last-minute scope churn and ensures consistent external communications.
acceptance_criteria: A single playbook doc exists with timeline templates for ship windows and cutoffs
Clear scope-freeze checklist defined for API, Console, and Runtime with owner assignments
Cut criteria enumerated (functional, perf, security, observability) with pass/fail thresholds
Release notes coordination template and delivery timeline agreed with comms and support
RACI for cross-team signoffs and a single rollback decision protocol documented
checklist: Draft playbook skeleton and timeline (owner: PM)
Workshop with Eng, Design, and SRE to validate cut criteria (owner: PM)
Publish release notes template and sample entry for a breaking/non-breaking change (owner: Docs)
Define monitoring dashboards and canary thresholds for runtime regressions (owner: SRE)
Lock API surface and create API compatibility test matrix (owner: Eng)
Console feature flag plan and staged rollout checklist (owner: Design)
Legal & compliance signoff checklist for Private customers (owner: Security)
Schedule post-mortem and lessons-learned slot for one week after ship (owner: PM)

decisions: Adopt single ship window approach (all three surfaces) rather than staggered ships to simplify comms and reduce fragmentation.
Enforce 'T-72 freeze' on new API surface changes; bugfixes allowed with approvals from PM+Eng lead.
Runtime kernel/quantization changes require additional perf signoff and a canary run on Dedicated capacity before broad rollout.
Release notes will publish a short summary + technical appendix; technical appendix maintained by Eng and Research for runtime changes.
risks: Late-breaking runtime perf regressions that only surface under production mixes; mitigated by expanded canary and post-canary smoke tests.
Scope creep in Console due to last-minute UX polish requests; mitigated by strict T-72 freeze and cherry-pick policy.
Mismatch between release notes technical detail level and Support/Customer needs; mitigate by early sample notes review with Support.
release_notes_plan: T-14 days: Draft entries collected from ENG/DES/RESEARCH into shared spreadsheet
T-7 days: Docs publishes internal pre-release notes for Support/Customer Success
T-3 days: Finalized public release notes and executive summary reviewed by PM+Comms
T+0 hours: Public release notes go live; product blog post and quickstart snippets published
T+1 day: Publish technical appendix and migration guidance for Dedicated/Private customers
rollouts_and_rollback: Staged rollout: Canary (5% traffic) -> Regional ramp (25%) -> Global ramp (100%)
Canary pass criteria: no SLO breaches, p95/p99 within defined bounds, error rate < 0.2% over 30m
Rollback trigger: sustained SLO breach >10 minutes or error spike >1% for 5 minutes; on-call SRE authorized to initiate automated rollback
Rollback procedure: pause traffic, revert to previous model binary or config, validate smoke tests, communicate to stakeholders via #release-ops
Post-rollback: schedule immediate incident review and freeze further rolling changes until RCA completed
